capture: s2-plan-compare / flights — live route London to Lisbon, 2026-11-10 to 2026-11-13

CORRECTION_to_finding_F28.original_claim: F-28 (capture 04): authentication unlocks exactly one capability on Google Travel — Track prices.
CORRECTION_to_finding_F28.what_this_capture_shows: 'Track prices' is present and offered on the SIGNED-OUT flights results page: 'Track prices from London to Lisbon departing 2026-11-10 and returning...'.
CORRECTION_to_finding_F28.corrected_claim: Track prices is gated per VERTICAL, not per account. It is absent from signed-out HOTELS and present on signed-out FLIGHTS.
CORRECTION_to_finding_F28.consequence_for_F29: F-29's contrast — Booking.com unlocks a discount, Google unlocks a capability — still holds for the hotels comparison where both were measured on the same vertical. But it can no longer be stated as a claim about the two PRODUCTS. It is a claim about their accommodation surfaces.
CORRECTION_to_finding_F28.how_this_was_caught: By capturing a second vertical on the same competitor rather than generalising from one. Recorded rather than quietly narrowed.

finding_F32_RANKING_IS_EXPLAINED.claim: Google Flights states its ranking criteria in plain language on the result set itself.
finding_F32_RANKING_IS_EXPLAINED.evidence_verbatim: Ranked based on price and convenience. Prices include required taxes + fees for 1 adult. Optional charges and bag fees may apply.

comparison.Booking.com: 'Commission paid on bookings, and other factors can affect property rankings' — discloses that commercial terms INFLUENCE ranking, without stating the criteria.
comparison.Google Flights: names the criteria (price and convenience) and scopes the price claim (1 adult, required taxes, optional bag fees excluded).

finding_F32_RANKING_IS_EXPLAINED.why_it_matters: This materially weakens the prior-round hypothesis that 'no competitor consistently explains its recommendations'. One competitor discloses commercial influence; another names its actual criteria. The claim needs restating before it is reused.

finding_F33_ACTIONABLE_ORIENTATION.claim: On a live route, Google states whether the current price is normal and when to buy — without requiring a booking, an account, or a commitment.
evidence_verbatim: The cheapest time to book is usually now, until Oct 17
finding_F33_ACTIONABLE_ORIENTATION.why_it_matters: 'Prices are currently typical' is the direct answer to a first-time traveller's central fear — am I being taken advantage of. 'Cheapest time to book is usually now, until Oct 17' converts that into a decision with a deadline. Neither transactional competitor said anything equivalent at any point in either journey captured.

finding_F34_A_FOURTH_AXIS_EXISTS.claim: Google Flights surfaces a comparison dimension that is neither price, quality proxy, nor distance: carbon emissions, expressed relative to the route average.
finding_F34_A_FOURTH_AXIS_EXISTS.important_scope_limit: This was observed as a DISPLAYED attribute per result. Whether emissions is a selectable SORT axis was not tested this pass. It is therefore NOT added to the 20-axis running total, which counts enumerated sort options only. OWED.
finding_F34_A_FOURTH_AXIS_EXISTS.why_it_matters_anyway: It demonstrates that a non-price, non-quality comparison dimension can be computed, displayed relative to a baseline, and understood at a glance. That is the structural proof-of-concept for an 'effort' or 'ease' axis, which F-25 established does not exist anywhere yet.

current_sort_state: Sorted by top flights — full option list NOT enumerated this pass. OWED before F-25's total can include the flights vertical.
our_product_decision_required: Decision required: F-34 is the most useful precedent in the round. Emissions is a computed, relative, non-price axis that travellers evidently tolerate. An 'effort' or 'ease' axis would work the same way — relative to a route baseline, shown per result. The objection that it cannot be computed is weakened by a working example.
Decision required: 'Prices are currently typical' costs nothing and requires no inventory. It is the single highest value-per-effort feature observed so far for Luma's stated user.
Decision required: Google explains its ranking criteria; Booking.com discloses commercial influence; Expedia explains nothing. Where does Luma sit, and can it explain a ranking it has not yet built?
not_observed: the handoff after selecting a flight — 'Book on Google' text not found; route untested
